title: Root-Traceable Procedural Dynamics / Constraint Geometry Falsification Attack

core_hypothesis.statement: Residue-coupled preserved distinction between Affecting and admissibility generates orientating chains whose whole-expression organization is more stable than projected trajectories.

new_or_candidate_operators.name: Residue-Coupled Preserved Distinction
new_or_candidate_operators.reading: Two processes remain residue-coupled while preserving non-identity.

new_or_candidate_operators.name: Admissibility-Class Equivalence
new_or_candidate_operators.reading: Two whole RT expressions belong to the same admissibility organization despite projected trajectory variation.

primary_test_claim.statement: If A <≠>_r a generates R_-i and Sigma_R, then whole-expression admissibility signatures should remain more stable than individual projected trajectories across perturbation, recurrence, and boundary-front variation.

falsification_attacks.question: Can <≠>_r be derived as a compression of the root expression, or does it introduce a second primitive?
falsification_attacks.failure_condition: <≠>_r cannot be traced to (E != 0) iff_R delta_a(E > 0).

falsification_attacks.question: Are projected trajectories actually more stable than whole RT expressions?
falsification_attacks.failure_condition: Trajectory-level markers outperform Sigma_R under recurrence and perturbation.

falsification_attacks.question: Do isolated components W_a, rho_D, chi, R_-i, or M_dom predict identity as well as or better than RT(Sigma_R)?
falsification_attacks.failure_condition: Any isolated component consistently equals or exceeds whole-expression classification stability.

falsification_attacks.question: Is quadrant volatility better explained as boundary-front dynamics rather than identity failure?
falsification_attacks.failure_condition: Quadrant jitter correlates with identity collapse rather than boundary interaction.

falsification_attacks.question: Does A <≠>_r a reliably generate residue-coupled orientation-event chains?
falsification_attacks.failure_condition: No recoverable -(i_k) ->_r -(i_k+1) structure appears under tested continuation.

success_criteria: All candidate operators maintain explicit root trace.
RT(Sigma_R) remains more stable than projected trajectory identity under tested perturbations.
Boundary-front interpretation explains quadrant volatility better than noise/error interpretation.
A <≠>_r a produces recoverable R_-i chains in tested models.
No isolated component outperforms the whole RT expression as identity marker.

governance_status.historical_note: This campaign records an earlier candidate form using <≠>_r. After PD_CG_PATCH_003_SUBSCRIPT_BASELINE_RESET, that qualifier is not the active default and must not be reused for promotion without a fresh direct comparison against bare <≠>.
